ei.title: BRINGING NEW LIFE TO OLD CITIES
ei.subject: 공통영어2

fullPassage: As cities age, neighborhoods can become old and lifeless, which may cause citizens to move away. When this happens, a collaboration between the local government and citizens is an effective way to revitalize the area. Let’s take a look at two projects in the Netherlands to find out what successful urban revitalization looks like. Wallisblok: The One-Euro Apartment Project Rotterdam, the second largest city in the Netherlands, is known for its modern architecture and busy port. By taking a ten-minute tram ride west from the city center, however, you can get to a more peaceful environment. Instead of crowded streets, you will see neighbors chatting in front of a modern residential structure and families spending time in its garden. The structure is a large apartment building called Wallisblok. Not that long ago, this area was very different, and nobody thought it could become a place where families would want to live. Yet that is exactly what happened. For years, the neighborhood was known for its high crime rates. Many apartments in Wallisblok were abandoned and then taken over by people who lived in them illegally. At first, the local government thought that the best solution was simply to tear the building down and build a new one in its place. However, having a limited budget, the government was unable to do so and had to come up with a new plan. The plan was to sell the empty apartments for one euro each. The only condition was that people who bought these apartments needed to renovate them. Although the new residents would have to pay for these renovations, the government’s plan soon attracted many applicants. Apparently, it was not just the idea of one-euro apartments that people found attractive. They were also excited by the opportunity to use their creativity to improve the building. In the end, 42 new families moved into Wallisblok. The government’s bold plan was a success. The residents transformed the old, worn-out building into 42 unique apartments with a community garden and rooftop terrace. The surrounding area soon began to improve as well. Today, Wallisblok is one of the most desirable places to live in Rotterdam. De Ceuvel: A Green-Technology Playground In the early 20th century, there was an area in the northern part of Amsterdam that was full of shipyards and factories. Over time, the shipyards closed down, and the work once done at the factories was moved abroad. As a result, the area was left abandoned and polluted for years. Wanting to do something to improve the area, the city purchased an abandoned shipyard called De Ceuvel. However, city officials did not know what to do with it. So they turned to the public for help by asking for plans that would achieve two primary goals. First, the plan had to include a method to clean up the land and turn it into a sustainable development. Second, it had to suggest a way to transform the site into a creative workspace. In the end, an architectural company submitted an innovative plan and was awarded a ten-year lease on the former shipyard. The plan was to turn the site into a sustainable office park. Since it was impossible to build foundations on the oily mud of the polluted land, the architects decided to use old, abandoned boats instead. They were able to purchase these at low prices from the boats’ owners. The architects created a small community that includes creative workspaces, studios, meeting rooms, cultural spaces, and even a café, all by upcycling the boats. Then, to connect the boats, wooden paths were built. In addition, special plants that purify polluted soil were planted across the site. Today, some people come to De Ceuvel to test new sustainable technologies such as bio-filters and water reuse systems. Many others come to experience this successful revitalization project in person. De Ceuvel is now known as one of the most active playgrounds for innovative green technology in all of Amsterdam. At the end of the lease, the project will also leave behind a more valuable piece of land for the next people who use it. These two examples of urban revitalization in the Netherlands required much more than a budget and a plan. Innovative thinking, creativity, community spirit, and cooperation were all vital to their success. These projects are great sources of inspiration for other cities that are looking to bring new life to abandoned areas.

questions.passage: By ①<u>taking</u> a ten-minute tram ride west from the city center, however, you can get to a more peaceful environment. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.analysis:
① taking: By taking a ten-minute tram ride — 전치사 By 뒤 동명사(V-ing) 적절
② chatting: you will see neighbors chatting — 지각동사 see + 목적어 + 현재분사(V-ing) 적절
③ calling → called: a large apartment building ___ Wallisblok에서 건물은 '~라고 불리는' 대상이므로 수동 관계. 과거분사 called(불리는)가 맞고, 능동의 현재분사 calling은 부적절 ←정답
④ could become: nobody thought it could become — 조동사 could + 동사원형 적절
det.tip: 명사를 뒤에서 수식할 때 '~되는/~받는' 수동 의미면 과거분사(p.p.)를 씁니다. building called ~ = ~라고 불리는 건물.

questions.passage: However, ①<u>had</u> a limited budget, the government was unable to do so and had to come up with a new plan.  The plan was ②<u>to sell</u> the empty apartments for one euro each.  The only condition was that people ③<u>who bought</u> these apartments needed to renovate them.  Although the new residents ④<u>would have to pay</u> for these renovations, the government’s plan soon attracted many applicants.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.analysis:
① had → having: 접속사 없이 두 개의 절을 이을 수 없다. 주절(the government was unable ~)의 주어와 능동 관계이므로 분사구문 Having a limited budget가 맞음. 정동사 had는 부적절 ←정답
② to sell: The plan was to sell — be동사의 보어로 to부정사 적절
③ who bought: people who bought these apartments — 주격 관계대명사 who + 과거동사 적절
④ would have to pay: the new residents would have to pay — 조동사 would + have to + 동사원형 적절
det.tip: 접속사 없이 문장 앞에 동사를 쓸 수 없습니다. 능동 분사구문은 Having ~ 형태입니다.

questions.passage: Apparently, it was not just the idea of one-euro apartments that people found attractive.  They were also ①<u>excited</u> by the opportunity to use their creativity ②<u>to improve</u> the building.  In the end, 42 new families ③<u>moved into</u> Wallisblok.  The government’s bold plan was a success.  The residents ④<u>transforming</u> the old, worn-out building into 42 unique apartments with a community garden and rooftop terrace.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.analysis:
① excited: They were also excited by ~ — be동사 + 과거분사 수동태(흥분되다) 적절
② to improve: the opportunity to use their creativity to improve — 앞 명사/목적을 나타내는 to부정사 적절
③ moved into: 42 new families moved into Wallisblok — 과거시제 정동사 적절
④ transforming → transformed: The residents ___ the old building에서 문장의 정동사가 필요. 과거시제 transformed가 맞고, 현재분사 transforming은 정동사가 될 수 없어 부적절 ←정답
det.tip: 주어 뒤 문장의 본동사 자리에는 현재분사(V-ing)가 아니라 시제를 갖춘 정동사가 와야 합니다.

questions.passage: Since it was impossible ①<u>to build</u> foundations on the oily mud of the polluted land, the architects decided to use old, abandoned boats instead.  They were able to purchase these at low prices from the boats’ owners.  The architects created a small community that ②<u>include</u> creative workspaces, studios, meeting rooms, cultural spaces, and even a café, all by upcycling the boats.  Then, ③<u>to connect</u> the boats, wooden paths were built.  In addition, special plants that purify polluted soil ④<u>were planted</u> across the site.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.analysis:
① to build: it was impossible to build foundations — 가주어 it, 진주어 to부정사 적절
② include → includes: a small community that ___ creative workspaces에서 주격 관계대명사 that의 선행사는 단수 community이므로 단수동사 includes가 맞음. 복수동사 include는 수 일치 위반 ←정답
③ to connect: to connect the boats, wooden paths were built — 목적을 나타내는 부사적 to부정사 적절
④ were planted: special plants that purify polluted soil were planted — 주어 plants(복수)에 맞는 복수 수동태 적절
det.tip: 주격 관계대명사의 동사는 선행사에 수를 맞춥니다. 선행사 community는 단수이므로 includes.

questions.passage: De Ceuvel: A Green-Technology Playground In the early 20th century, there was an area in the northern part of Amsterdam that was ①<u>full</u> of shipyards and factories.  Over time, the shipyards ②<u>closed down</u>, and the work once done at the factories was moved abroad.  As a result, the area was left abandoned and ③<u>clean</u> for years.  Wanting to do something to improve the area, the city ④<u>purchased</u> an abandoned shipyard called De Ceuvel.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.analysis:
① full(가득한): 조선소와 공장으로 '가득했던' 지역이라는 문맥에 적절
② closed down(문을 닫았다): 시간이 지나 조선소들이 '문을 닫았다'는 문맥에 적절
③ clean(깨끗한) → polluted(오염된): 조선소가 문을 닫고 일자리가 해외로 옮겨져 지역이 '버려지고 오염된' 채 방치되었다는 흐름이므로 polluted가 맞음. clean은 정반대 ←정답
④ purchased(매입했다): the city purchased an abandoned shipyard — 그 도시가 버려진 조선소를 '매입했다'는 문맥에 적절
det.tip: '버려진(abandoned)'과 나란히 쓰여 여러 해 방치된 상태를 나타내는 부정적 단어는 polluted(오염된)입니다.

questions.passage: Today, some people come to De Ceuvel to ①<u>test</u> new sustainable technologies such as bio-filters and water reuse systems.  Many others come to experience this ②<u>failed revitalization</u> project in person.  De Ceuvel is now known as one of the most active playgrounds for innovative green technology in all of Amsterdam.  At the end of the lease, the project will also leave behind a more ③<u>valuable</u> piece of land for the next people who use it.  These two examples of urban revitalization in the Netherlands required much more than a budget and a plan.  Innovative thinking, creativity, community spirit, and cooperation were all ④<u>vital</u> to their success.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.analysis:
① test(시험하다): 사람들이 '지속 가능한 신기술을 시험하러' 온다는 문맥에 적절
② failed revitalization(실패한 재생) → successful revitalization(성공적인 재생): 사람들이 직접 체험하러 오고 도시 재생의 모범이 된 프로젝트이므로 '성공적인 재생'이 맞음. failed는 정반대 ←정답
③ valuable(가치 있는): 임대 종료 시 더 '가치 있는' 땅을 남긴다는 문맥에 적절
④ vital(필수적인): 혁신적 사고와 협력이 성공에 '필수적'이었다는 문맥에 적절
det.tip: De Ceuvel은 사람들이 체험하러 오는 도시 재생의 모범 사례이므로 successful(성공적인)이 어울립니다.

det.analysis: T: 본문 'By taking a ten-minute tram ride west from the city center, however, you can get to a more peaceful environment.'에서 도심에서 서쪽으로 10분 트램을 타면 더 평화로운 환경에 이를 수 있다고 명시되어 있다.

det.analysis: T: 본문 'Since it was impossible to build foundations on the oily mud of the polluted land, the architects decided to use old, abandoned boats instead.'에서 오염된 땅에 기초를 세울 수 없어 대신 버려진 배들을 사용하기로 했다고 명시되어 있다.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 정부가 시민에게 요청한 계획이 달성해야 할 두 가지 것.
det.analysis:
① goals(목표): 뒤에 First(첫째)~, Second(둘째)~로 두 가지 목표(땅 정화 + 창의적 작업 공간 조성)를 제시하므로 '두 가지 주요 목표'가 자연스럽다 ←정답
② rules(규칙): 달성(achieve)의 대상으로 부적절
③ costs(비용): 계획이 달성할 대상으로 어색함
④ dangers(위험): 긍정적 계획의 목적과 어울리지 않음
det.tip: 빈칸 뒤 First ~, Second ~ 구조가 두 가지 goals(목표)를 나열하고 있음을 알려줍니다.

questions.passage: As cities age, neighborhoods can become old and lifeless, which may cause citizens to move away.  When this happens, a collaboration between the local government and citizens is an effective way to revitalize the area.  Let’s take a look at two projects in the Netherlands to find out what successful urban revitalization looks like.  Wallisblok: The One-Euro Apartment Project Rotterdam, the second largest city in the Netherlands, is known for its modern architecture and busy port.  By taking a ten-minute tram ride west from the city center, however, you can get to a more peaceful environment.  Instead of crowded streets, you will see neighbors chatting in front of a modern residential structure and families spending time in its garden.  The structure is a large apartment building called Wallisblok.  Not that long ago, this area was very different, and nobody thought it could become a place where families would want to live.  Yet that is exactly what happened.  For years, the neighborhood was known for its high crime rates.  Many apartments in Wallisblok were abandoned and then taken over by people who lived in them illegally.  At first, the local government thought that the best solution was simply to tear the building down and build a new one in its place.  However, having a limited budget, the government was unable to do so and had to come up with a new plan.  The plan was to sell the empty apartments for one euro each.  The only condition was that people who bought these apartments needed to renovate them.  Although the new residents would have to pay for these renovations, the government’s plan soon attracted many applicants.  Apparently, it was not just the idea of one-euro apartments that people found attractive.  They were also excited by the opportunity to use their creativity to improve the building.  In the end, 42 new families moved into Wallisblok.  The government’s bold plan was a success.  The residents transformed the old, worn-out building into 42 unique apartments with a community garden and rooftop terrace.  The surrounding area soon began to improve as well.  Today, Wallisblok is one of the most desirable places to live in Rotterdam.  De Ceuvel: A Green-Technology Playground In the early 20th century, there was an area in the northern part of Amsterdam that was full of shipyards and factories.  Over time, the shipyards closed down, and the work once done at the factories was moved abroad.  As a result, the area was left abandoned and polluted for years.  Wanting to do something to improve the area, the city purchased an abandoned shipyard called De Ceuvel.  However, city officials did not know what to do with it.  So they turned to the public for help by asking for plans that would achieve two primary goals.  First, the plan had to include a method to clean up the land and turn it into a sustainable development.  Second, it had to suggest a way to transform the site into a creative workspace.  In the end, an architectural company submitted an innovative plan and was awarded a ten-year lease on the former shipyard.  The plan was to turn the site into a sustainable office park.  Since it was impossible to build foundations on the oily mud of the polluted land, the architects decided to use old, abandoned boats instead.  They were able to purchase these at low prices from the boats’ owners.  The architects created a small community that includes creative workspaces, studios, meeting rooms, cultural spaces, and even a café, all by upcycling the boats.  Then, to connect the boats, wooden paths were built.  In addition, special plants that purify polluted soil were planted across the site.  Today, some people come to De Ceuvel to test new sustainable technologies such as bio-filters and water reuse systems.  Many others come to experience this successful revitalization project in person.  De Ceuvel is now known as one of the most active playgrounds for innovative green technology in all of Amsterdam.  At the end of the lease, the project will also leave behind a more valuable piece of land for the next people who use it.  These two examples of urban revitalization in the Netherlands required much more than a budget and a plan.  Innovative thinking, creativity, community spirit, and cooperation were all vital to their success.

det.analysis:
